title: Boss Rounds
tagline: The interviewer moves the dials. Defend your answer anyway.
story: The question has crossed every stop on the journey, and the interviewer starts changing the constraints halfway through your answer. Each boss round mixes chapters: a retrieval design that must survive an access review, an assistant that must be fast, cheap and available at once, and an agent platform where tools, peers and workflows share one set of rules. You are scored on clarifying first, choosing for stated dials, naming what flips the choice, and saying how you would know it works.
oneLiner: Six mixed rounds where every answer crosses chapters, so you practise choosing, flipping and defending under changing constraints.
youWillLearn: Carry one design across chapters: ingest, chunk, retrieve, guard and authorise a RAG answer, and say where each choice constrains the next
Trade latency, cost and availability against each other and against correctness and tenant isolation
Place functions, MCP servers, A2A peers, workflows and handoffs by ownership boundary, task shape and risk
Answer an open interview prompt with the five Dial-and-Defend steps inside a time box
Say out loud what flips your choice, how you would detect failure and which metric you would watch
Pull in the operating chapters (identity, evaluation, observability, governance) when a design has to ship
Revise with cross-chapter rapid-fire contrasts in the flashcard deck

flashcards.front: Pre-filter, post-filter, live check: what does each do to the top k?
flashcards.back: Pre-filter applies the caller's access rule inside the search, so top k holds only readable chunks. Post-filter fetches first, then drops, and starves k. Live check asks the source at query time: freshest, slowest.

flashcards.front: Part number versus paraphrase: which retrieval leg wins each?
flashcards.back: Keyword (BM25) wins exact identifiers, dates and names. Dense vectors win paraphrase and meaning. Hybrid runs both in parallel and fuses the ranks with RRF. Query rewrites can drop identifiers, so test them.

flashcards.front: RRF versus a weighted score mix: when do you pick which?
flashcards.back: RRF fuses ranks, so it needs no score calibration and works out of the box. A convex combination of normalised scores can beat it but needs labelled examples to tune the weight.

flashcards.front: What can a reranker not do?
flashcards.back: It reorders a shortlist and cannot find a document the first stage missed. The Azure semantic ranker reranks only the top 50 of the BM25 or RRF results, so fix recall before ranking.

flashcards.front: Parent-child versus contextual retrieval: how does each repair a chunk that lost its context?
flashcards.back: Parent-child matches small children and returns the larger parent. Contextual retrieval prepends LLM-written context to each chunk before embedding and BM25. Anthropic measured 35%, 49% and 67% fewer top-20 failures, the last with reranking.

flashcards.front: Why is re-embedding done blue-green and not in place?
flashcards.back: Vectors from different embedding models are not comparable, and Azure embedding models cannot be upgraded in place. Build a second index, backfill, compare on a golden set, repoint an alias, keep the old index for rollback.

flashcards.front: Prompt Shields, spotlighting, groundedness detection: what does each catch?
flashcards.back: Prompt Shields classifies user and document attacks (GA). Spotlighting marks untrusted text so the model discounts instructions in it. Groundedness detection (preview) checks answer claims against sources. Each is probabilistic.

flashcards.front: Security filters versus native ACL scopes in Azure AI Search, as of 2026-10-13?
flashcards.back: Security filters are GA: you resolve groups and store ACL strings on each chunk. Native ACL and RBAC scopes, Purview labels and SharePoint ACLs are preview: the user's token goes in the `x-ms-query-source-authorization` header.

flashcards.front: What does a token carry when the user belongs to 300 groups?
flashcards.back: An overage indicator instead of the group list, because a JWT lists at most 200 groups. Call Graph `transitiveMemberOf` (999 per page at most) and fail closed on any error.

flashcards.front: What does a citation prove, and what does it not?
flashcards.back: It proves provenance: which chunk a claim came from. It does not prove the claim is supported or true. Pair citations with a groundedness check, a score cutoff and abstention.

flashcards.front: Slow first word or slow finish: which lever for each?
flashcards.back: First token is queueing plus prefill: shorten or cache the prompt. Total time is mostly output tokens: cap, trim and stream. OpenAI says halving output may halve latency, halving the prompt about 1% to 5%.

flashcards.front: Prompt cache versus semantic cache: what comes back and what is the risk?
flashcards.back: A prompt cache reuses KV state for an identical prefix, still runs the model and never changes the answer. A semantic cache returns a stored answer for a similar prompt, which can be wrong or belong to another user.

flashcards.front: Prompt cache prices on GPT-5.6 and later?
flashcards.back: Cache write 1.25x and read 0.1x of the uncached input rate (0.05x on GPT-6.1 Sol). One write plus nine reads costs 2.15x against 10x uncached. The minimum prefix is 1,024 visible tokens.

flashcards.front: `cached_tokens` is 0 on a long prompt. First suspect?
flashcards.back: The first 1,024 tokens differ between requests: a timestamp, user id or reordered tools near the top. Put stable content first, volatile content last, and keep tool lists in a fixed order.

flashcards.front: PTU, Priority, Batch, Flex: one line each.
flashcards.back: PTU reserves throughput and bills it whether used or not. Priority is a faster tier on standard quota. Batch is 50% off with a 24-hour target. Flex (preview) is 50% off with no SLA.

flashcards.front: Why can an Azure OpenAI 429 appear below your real usage?
flashcards.back: The TPM check counts prompt plus `max_tokens` (plus `best_of`) up front, so an oversized `max_tokens` eats quota. Capacity throttling and a temporary rate-limit adjustment on Standard are other causes.

flashcards.front: Retry, hedge, circuit breaker: which problem does each solve?
flashcards.back: Retry fixes a transient error: backoff, jitter, a cap. A hedge sends a second copy of a slow call to cut tail latency and needs idempotency. A breaker stops calling a failing dependency so it can recover.

flashcards.front: Spillover versus regional failover on Azure?
flashcards.back: Spillover sends non-200 overflow from a PTU deployment to a standard deployment in the same resource. Foundry has no automatic regional failover: you build, size and test the second region yourself.

flashcards.front: Router versus cascade: who decides and what does each cost?
flashcards.back: A router picks one model before the call and can misroute. A cascade tries a cheap model and escalates when a check fails, so hard queries pay twice. Azure model router Balanced stays within about 1% to 2% of top quality.

flashcards.front: Chat Completions versus Responses: who holds the state?
flashcards.back: Chat Completions is stateless: you resend the messages. Responses can store state server-side (30 days by default) and chain with `previous_response_id`, which bills the earlier input tokens again.

flashcards.front: Tools, resources, prompts: who controls each?
flashcards.back: Tools are model-controlled, resources are application-controlled and prompts are user-controlled. Put side effects in tools, attachable context in resources and slash-command templates in prompts.

flashcards.front: MCP, A2A, agent-as-tool: which crosses which boundary?
flashcards.back: MCP joins an agent to tools and data. A2A joins independent, opaque agents across an ownership boundary using tasks. Agent-as-tool is a plain in-process call inside one codebase. Real systems combine them.

flashcards.front: Why is token passthrough forbidden in MCP?
flashcards.back: A server must not accept or forward a token that was not issued for it. Exchange the inbound token for a downstream token with the right audience (on-behalf-of), or the server becomes a confused deputy.

flashcards.front: What did MCP revision 2026-07-28 change about connections?
flashcards.back: It removed protocol sessions: no `initialize` handshake and no `Mcp-Session-Id` header. Every request carries protocol version and client capabilities in `_meta`, and servers must implement `server/discover`.

flashcards.front: Handoff versus supervisor: who owns the user conversation?
flashcards.back: In a handoff the receiving agent takes ownership and no central orchestrator exists, so cap the turns to stop ping-pong loops. A supervisor keeps control and calls specialists as tools, so one agent owns the conversation.

flashcards.front: Agent, Harness Agent, Workflow: what does each add?
flashcards.back: An agent is one model loop with tools. A Harness Agent is the same agent with todos, plan and execute modes, standing approvals and history persistence on by default. A workflow is a graph where your code fixes the order.

flashcards.front: Checkpoint, session, background response: what survives a restart?
flashcards.back: A workflow checkpoint, written per superstep, holds executor state, pending messages and requests, and shared state. A session holds conversation state. A background response is a provider-held run you poll with a continuation token.

flashcards.front: When do you add a second agent?
flashcards.back: Start with one. Add agents when a named dial forces it: breadth beyond one context, tool overload or isolation. Anthropic measured about 15x chat tokens for multi-agent. Cognition warns that parallel writers make conflicting decisions.

flashcards.front: An A2A task is COMPLETED and the user wants a change. What is the next call?
flashcards.back: Terminal tasks cannot restart. Send a new message with the same `contextId`, optionally with `referenceTaskIds`, and the server creates a new task. Task ids are always server-generated.

flashcards.front: What must hold across a tool-approval round trip in Agent Framework?
flashcards.back: The same `AgentSession`. By default an approval response authorizes a call only when it matches a pending request in that session. Disabling that binding can let a fabricated approval through. [[r51]]

flashcards.front: What agent types does Foundry Agent Service offer, and which protocols do hosted agents expose?
flashcards.back: Prompt agents, voice-based prompt agents and hosted agents. Hosted agents expose Responses, Invocations, Invocations WebSocket, Activity and A2A, and one agent can expose several. [[r52]] [[r53]]

flashcards.front: Who holds the credentials: an Entra agent identity or its blueprint?
flashcards.back: The blueprint. An agent identity is a service principal (`ServiceIdentity`) with no credentials of its own. In OBO the user is the token subject and the agent is the actor. In S2S the agent is the subject. [[r55]]

flashcards.front: When did Agent 365 reach GA, and for whom?
flashcards.back: 2026-05-01, for the Commercial segment, licensed per user. It observes, governs and secures agents through a registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft Entra, Purview and Defender. [[r54]]

flashcards.front: What are Foundry's three evaluation stages?
flashcards.back: Base model selection, pre-production evaluation and post-production monitoring. Offline golden sets gate releases, and online monitoring catches drift that the golden set never held. [[r56]]

flashcards.front: Why run the AI Red Teaming Agent more than once?
flashcards.back: Its Attack Success Rate (successful attacks over total attacks) is scored by a generative model, so results can be non-deterministic and include false positives. Review samples and track the trend. Preview. [[r57]]

flashcards.front: Which spans does Agent Framework emit, and is content captured by default?
flashcards.back: `invoke_agent <name>`, `chat <model>` and `execute_tool <function>`. Instrumentation should not capture prompts and outputs by default: they are opt-in attributes. The GenAI conventions carry Development status. [[r58]]

flashcards.front: Which EU AI Act dates matter for GenAI teams?
flashcards.back: In force 2024-08-01. Prohibitions and AI literacy from 2025-02-02. GPAI obligations from 2025-08-02. Systems placed on the market before 2026-08-02 have until 2026-12-02 for Article 50(2) marking under the AI Omnibus. [[r59]]

flashcards.front: NIST AI 600-1 in one line?
flashcards.back: The Generative AI Profile of the NIST AI RMF, released 2024-07-26. It lists twelve GenAI risks, with prompt injection and data poisoning under information security. [[r60]]

glossary.def: The five-step answer method: clarify the dials, list the options, pick and say what flips the pick, name the failure modes, name the metrics and rollout.
A mixed practice round that crosses chapters and ends in an open interview prompt with unspecified dials.

An access or metadata filter applied inside the search so the top k holds only permitted chunks. Azure AI Search offers `preFilter`, `postFilter` and `strictPostFilter` (preview) for vector queries [[r5]].
Dropping results after retrieval. Cheap to build, but it starves the top k under selective access and lets denied text reach rerankers, caches and logs.
A permission lookup against the source system at query time on the shortlist: the freshest answer at the cost of latency and source load.
Merges ranked lists by summing a reciprocal of each document's rank per list, so it needs no score calibration [[r7]].
Declining to answer when retrieval is empty or weak, instead of letting the model improvise.
Provider-side reuse of the KV state of a repeated prefix. It changes cost and time to first token, not the answer [[r19]].
A cache that returns a stored answer when a new prompt embeds close enough to an earlier one. It needs partitioning by user or permission scope [[r23]].
Sending overflow requests from a provisioned deployment to a standard deployment in the same resource [[r29]].
Stops calls to a failing dependency for a cool-down period so it can recover and callers fail fast.
A duplicate of a slow request sent to another replica to cut tail latency. It needs idempotent calls and costs extra requests.
One round of a graph workflow in Agent Framework: messages move between executors, and a checkpoint is written at the end [[r50]].
An agent whose prompts, tools and internal state stay hidden from its caller. A2A peers interact only through tasks and messages [[r42]].
Forwarding a token that was not issued for your server to a downstream service. MCP forbids it [[r39]].

claims.text: Azure AI Search says querying over product codes, highly specialized jargon, dates and people's names performs better with keyword search because it identifies exact matches.
In Azure AI Search, RRF runs whenever two or more queries execute in parallel, for example a text query plus a vector query.
The Azure semantic ranker reranks only the top 50 results of BM25 or RRF and cannot rerun the query to find new documents.
Azure AI Search vectorFilterMode offers preFilter, postFilter and strictPostFilter (preview), and indexes created before about 2023-10-15 default to postFilter.
The blob indexer detects changes through LastModified, does not track deletes by default, and does not re-index a renamed ADLS Gen2 directory because LastModified does not change.
OpenAI and Azure advise reserving at least 25,000 tokens for reasoning and output when starting with a reasoning model.
Native ACL queries pass the user's Entra token in the x-ms-query-source-authorization header, and from 2025-11-01-preview a missing user token returns only public documents. Preview as of 2026-10-13.

Azure AI Search lists four document-level access approaches: security filters, POSIX-like ACL and RBAC scopes, Purview sensitivity labels and SharePoint ACLs. The last three are preview as of 2026-10-13.
An Entra token carries at most 200 groups in a JWT, and above that an overage indicator replaces the groups claim.
Azure groundedness detection is preview as of 2026-10-13 and offers domain (Medical, Generic) and task (Summarization, QnA) options.
On GPT-5.6 and later a cache write costs 1.25x and a read 0.1x the uncached input rate (0.05x for reads on GPT-6.1 Sol), so one write plus nine reads costs 2.15x versus 10x uncached.
On OpenAI and Azure GPT-5.6 and later the minimum cacheable prefix is 1,024 visible input tokens and prompt_cache_options.ttl supports only 30m.
On Azure before GPT-5.6, a cache hit needs an identical first 1,024 tokens and hits count in 128-token increments.
A 2025 audit (ICML 2025) detected global cache sharing across users in seven providers, including OpenAI, through response timing.
In the API Management semantic cache policy a lower score-threshold is stricter, Microsoft suggests starting near 0.05, above 0.2 may cause mismatches, and vary-by partitions the cache.
OpenAI's latency guide says cutting 50% of output tokens may cut about 50% of latency while cutting 50% of the prompt may give only 1% to 5%.
Responses are stored by default for 30 days, and previous_response_id bills the earlier input tokens again.
PTU capacity is held and billed whether or not requests arrive, and cached tokens do not consume PTU capacity.
Spillover sends non-200 overflow from a provisioned deployment to a standard deployment in the same resource, per request with the x-ms-spillover-deployment header.
Azure's TPM check counts prompt plus max_tokens plus best_of up front, and RPM is enforced over 1 or 10 second windows.
Foundry does not provide automatic failover. Approximate RTO is minutes for hot/hot, 30 minutes to 2 hours for hot/warm and 2 to 8 hours for hot/cold.
OpenAI Batch gives a 50% discount with completion_window 24h, up to 50,000 requests and 200 MB per file.

MCP revision 2026-07-28 removed protocol sessions, the Mcp-Session-Id header and the initialize handshake, every request carries protocolVersion and clientCapabilities in _meta, and servers must implement server/discover.
MCP servers must implement RFC 9728 protected resource metadata, clients must send the RFC 8707 resource parameter, and servers must not accept tokens not issued for them.
Anthropic says a typical five-server MCP setup can use about 55k tokens of tool definitions, tool search cuts that by over 85 percent, and tool selection degrades past 30 to 50 tools.
A2A terminal task states are COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED and REJECTED, the interrupted states are INPUT_REQUIRED and AUTH_REQUIRED, and task ids are server-generated.
MCP is vertical and connects one agent to tools and resources, while A2A is horizontal and connects independent agents across a boundary. They are used together.
Anthropic reports agents use about 4x and multi-agent systems about 15x the tokens of chat, and that its multi-agent system beat single-agent Claude Opus 4 by 90.2% on an internal research eval.

Workflow checkpoints are written at the end of each superstep and capture executor state, pending messages, pending requests and responses, and shared state. Pending human requests are re-emitted on restore.
A hosted agent endpoint serves one version with 100 percent of traffic and traffic splitting is not supported, so a canary is a second agent.
Hosted agent sandbox sizes are 0.5 vCPU with 1 GiB, 1 vCPU with 2 GiB and 2 vCPU with 4 GiB, and the docs advise the next size when sustained peaks pass about 70 percent of allocation.
Every Entra agent identity and blueprint needs at least one sponsor. Owners are optional.
A token whose audience is the MCP server URL instead of the downstream resource id, such as https://storage.azure.com, fails even when RBAC is correct.
Foundry Workflows (preview) retire on 2026-12-01 and classic agents on 2027-03-31.

EU AI Act dates: prohibitions and AI literacy 2025-02-02, general-purpose AI obligations 2025-08-02, Article 50 transparency from 2026-08-02, and Annex III high-risk moved to 2027-12-02 by the Omnibus.
Microsoft Graph transitiveMemberOf returns 100 items per page by default and at most 999.
In MT-Bench, consistency after swapping answer order was 65.0 percent for GPT-4, 46.2 for GPT-3.5 and 23.8 for Claude-v1, and a reference answer cut math grading failures from 14 of 20 to 3 of 20.
Patch image models use ceil(w/32) x ceil(h/32) patches times a 1.2 multiplier, so a 1024 x 1024 image at high detail costs 1,229 tokens.
Realtime audio costs 1 token per 100 ms of user audio and 1 per 50 ms of assistant audio, the conversation is resent each turn and retention_ratio defaults to 1.0.
The @trace_function decorator records parameters and return values regardless of the sensitive-data and content-capture flags.
